checks: Legacy account/v1 access remains compatible, but legacy session cannot enter person gate.
Verified provider callback binds stable subject once under concurrent first login; two agencies and reader remain separate, and identity grants no owner action.
Only explicitly allowlisted unprovisioned operator gets legacy login; it cannot enter person gate. Bound operator uses v2, and unprovisioned staff get no fallback.
Actual portal renders verified and legacy identity states at desktop and 390px widths, with keyboard-accessible fresh sign-in.
Reused email with another provider subject, unsupported OTP type, invalid token and unconfirmed email deny sign-in and clear prior cookie.
Direct service-role disable/re-enable and company A→B→A invalidate prior cookie epochs; fresh same-person sign-in observes new epoch.
Email reuse cannot retarget v2 API or any of seven account pages; old cookie gets recovery UI and same provider can freshly authenticate renamed account.
Committed login reply loss does not mint fallback authority; fresh OTP reconciles the same immutable binding.
Deletion/recreation creates a new account incarnation while tombstones prevent old provider binding or cookie revival.
Unavailable identity RPC holds both API and rendered account without email fallback, with bounded recovery messages.

layers.portal: actual built Next callback, cookies, APIs and rendered pages
